edges.effect_quant: Prospective cohort data point in more than one direction, so no single pooled effect estimate is reliable enough to summarize cleanly.
edges.mechanism: This factor changes substrate delivery, microbial competition, short-chain fatty-acid production, or early-life colonization patterns in the gut. Those changes are most directly linked to Gut microbiome diversity when the endpoint is microbial composition, barrier function, or a gut-mediated immune phenotype.
edges.summary: In general adult, prospective cohort data suggest that kombucha tracks with mixed effects on gut microbiome diversity. Direct human evidence is thin here, so the best reading is cautious and largely driven by adjacency, plausibility, and the absence of stable high-quality trials.
edges.caveats: This is a thin-evidence edge. Direct human outcome trials are sparse, so the safest interpretation is uncertainty rather than a confident positive or negative claim.
